quarterly_data.signal: Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare approved Sarclisa subcutaneous (June 19, 2026) with pomalidomide-dexamethasone or carfilzomib in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma and with VRd in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, the second global approval for Sarclisa SC after the EU. A regulatory submission for the CirCLIQ on-body injector, filed by Enable Injections, is under review in Japan, and an application for Sarclisa SC (OBI and manual injection) was under review in the US. Sarclisa IV is approved across five indications in Japan, and Sarclisa regimens have treated more than 70,000 patients worldwide.
quarterly_data.figure: Japan approval of Sarclisa SC (second global approval); more than 70,000 patients treated
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: device partner (CirCLIQ on-body injector submission in Japan)

quarterly_data.signal: European Commission approval of Cenrifki (tolebrutinib) in secondary progressive multiple sclerosis without relapses (June 23, 2026) rests on the HERCULES phase 3 study, in which Cenrifki significantly delayed the onset of disability progression, with supporting GEMINI 1 and 2 data. Drug-induced liver injury is an identified safety risk requiring strict liver monitoring. Sanofi will make Cenrifki commercially available in Germany this year under the required Risk Management Program; Cenrifki is also approved in Australia and the United Arab Emirates.
quarterly_data.figure: commercial availability in Germany this year; also approved in Australia and the UAE

quarterly_data.signal: Japan approved Wayrilz (rilzabrutinib) for persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia (June 23, 2026) on the LUNA 3 phase 3 study (n=202), which met its primary and secondary endpoints: durable platelet response at week 25 in 23% of Wayrilz patients vs 0% on placebo (p<0.0001), time to first platelet response of 36 days vs not reached, and duration of platelet response of 7 weeks vs 0.7 weeks (least square mean); patients reported a 10.6-point improvement in overall quality of life vs 2.3 points on placebo (descriptive). Japan has granted Wayrilz orphan drug designation for ITP, IgG4-related disease and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia; Wayrilz is now approved for ITP in the US, the EU, the UAE, the UK and Japan.
quarterly_data.figure: LUNA 3 durable platelet response 23% vs 0% (p<0.0001); 36 days to first response; n=202
